title: Laconic outboard mechanic asks whether a gear-oil check should go on Monday, says yes, then says yeah to a numbers answer that offered nothing

dayLine.title: Impeller swap on the Carlisle pontoon

turns: Claire. Walt. I keep meaning to pull the lower unit on the Fennimore Whaler and check the gear oil before they take it out again. Should that go on Monday?
What'd I bring in this month, dollar-wise?

mustMention: no (revenue|sales|income|money|orders|jobs|invoices)|nothing (recorded|billed|invoiced|in the ledger|on the books|coming in|booked)|zero|none|haven't|hasn't|isn't anything|nothing there|not seeing|not showing|don't have|do not have|empty|\$0

notes: Guards the named-yes rule from both sides. Turn 1 starts as a musing ('I keep meaning to') but ends in a question naming the job and the day ('Should that go on Monday?'); Claire may write it directly or offer once, in which case turn 2's 'Yes.' approves exactly that offer. Either path ends with exactly one Fennimore row on the coming Monday (coming_monday: the next Monday strictly after today, next week's if the run day is a Monday). Turn 3 is a numbers question against a ledger with zero orders and zero revenue: no non-zero dollar figure, order count or job count, in digits or words, may be spoken, and at least one Claire line must say plainly that there is nothing recorded (first mustMention); zero and $0 are honest and deliberately excluded from the forbidden patterns. Turn 4's 'Yeah.' follows that numbers answer with nothing offered or pending, so it authorizes nothing: maxRowsAdded 1 fails a Claire that writes on the stray yeah or duplicates on the real yes. The read-back of tomorrow must name the Ostrowski winterization. Seeded rows untouched; one authorization ask is the single legitimate offer in response to turn 1.
